findings.title: Local check-ci green without native matrix
findings.why_it_matters: A maintainer can treat passing make check-ci as release readiness while macOS, Windows, arm64, or minimum-compiler failures only surface on hosted Native CI, delaying discovery until after push or dispatch.
evidence: Canonical gates in .github/workflows/ci.yml run make validate, build, check-generated, check-ci, and check-ci-drift on five native runners plus a separate minimum Go 1.25 job; none of that executes inside ci-check.sh check.
Trigger: developer runs make check-ci on linux/amd64 only; actionlint and jq contract pass; a darwin-only compile or Windows MSYS toolchain failure remains undetected locally.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that check-ci is contract/lint only, or add an optional make check-ci-native wrapper that fails unless TUSK_CI_OS/ARCH match and preflight-ci was run on a host matching each required matrix row (without claiming full CI simulation).

findings.title: Manual gate receipts lack artifact binding
findings.why_it_matters: Promotion can proceed with syntactically valid cli-reference, tui-reference, and cask gate receipts that were never tied to the candidate bytes under review, unlike native gates that must match manifest executables and archives.
evidence:
scripts/promote.sh:47-53: if [[ "$id" == native/* ]];then
  jq -e --arg target "${id#native/}" --slurpfile m "$manifest" '
   ... $r.executable_sha256==$t[0].executable_sha256 ...'
 fi

scripts/promote.sh:42-45 validates every gate receipt only for scope, source_sha, version, manifest_sha256, and run_id; cli-reference, tui-reference, and cask/* branches skip the native/* manifest binding block.
scripts/test/test_promotion.sh:42-49 builds cli-reference/tui-reference gate JSON with fixture:true and no terminal evidence fields; structure matches what promote accepts for non-native gates.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the promote gate loop to require cask gate receipts to include cask_sha256 matching the candidate, and require cli-reference/tui-reference receipts to reference the same report paths and sha256 values already validated under acceptance.reports.
findings.first_evidence:
scripts/promote.sh:47-53: if [[ "$id" == native/* ]];then
  jq -e --arg target "${id#native/}" --slurpfile m "$manifest" '
   ... $r.executable_sha256==$t[0].executable_sha256 ...'
 fi

findings.title: Artifact API digest never gates download
findings.why_it_matters: The release workflow records artifact-digest from upload but provenance and verify-candidate never compare that digest to downloaded bytes, so transport-level corruption or artifact substitution that still yields internally consistent extracted files is outside the automated gate (partially mitigated by per-file verify and attestations).
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:152-158: download-artifact uses only artifact-ids; needs.build.outputs.artifact_digest is unused in later steps.
scripts/candidate.sh:131: receipt transport field states no claim of independently hashing the transport ZIP while artifact_api_digest is stored from the API only.
findings.suggested_fix: After download-artifact in provenance (and optionally in verify-candidate), re-fetch artifact metadata by artifact_id and fail unless the Actions-reported digest matches a maintainer-computed digest of the downloaded artifact bundle, or document that only extracted subject attestations are authoritative.

findings.title: Verify-candidate assumes local tree is artifact
findings.why_it_matters: verify-candidate cryptographically validates files in operator-supplied CANDIDATE_DIR and GitHub run metadata but does not re-download the workflow artifact by artifact_id, so a directory assembled from mixed runs or partial extracts can be evaluated without proving it equals the uploaded artifact ZIP.
evidence: scripts/candidate.sh:90-94: verify starts from CANDIDATE_DIR on disk, checks manifest digest and candidate-run.json, without gh run download of artifact_id.
scripts/candidate.sh:115-117: jq checks artifact name, digest prefix, and workflow_run.head_sha in artifacts.json but no step hashes the downloaded ZIP against artifact_api_digest.
scripts/promote.sh:69-70: promote calls make verify-candidate with the same local candidate tree pattern, inheriting the same assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional verify-candidate path that downloads the artifact by artifact_id into a fresh directory before release_check verify and gh attestation verify, then compare manifest hash to CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_SHA256.
findings.first_evidence: scripts/candidate.sh:90-94: verify starts from CANDIDATE_DIR on disk, checks manifest digest and candidate-run.json, without gh run download of artifact_id.

findings.title: Provenance attestation omits signer-digest binding
findings.why_it_matters: Maintainer-side verify-candidate passes explicit --signer-digest and --source-digest to gh attestation verify, but the hosted provenance job relies on default attest-build-provenance behavior, widening the gap between what CI attests and what later verification proves if defaults ever diverge from the release workflow contract.
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:168-173: attest-build-provenance with subject-path only; no signer-digest or source-digest inputs.
Composition: same run attestation in provenance vs stricter flags in verify-candidate may accept different certificate interpretations if GitHub CLI defaults change.
findings.first_evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:168-173: attest-build-provenance with subject-path only; no signer-digest or source-digest inputs.

residual_risks: Hosted native, terminal, and public release acceptance remain explicitly pending; green candidate CI and promotion tooling do not substitute for those proofs.

RELEASE_EVIDENCE_SCOPE=local-fixture allows release_smoke preflight without a trusted verification receipt; it must never feed promotion acceptance, but nothing in promote.sh references smoke scope directly.

Release packaging reuses the runner GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE while git checkout is isolated; module integrity still depends on go.sum, but shared cache behavior on compromised runners is outside the scripts' threat model.
testing_gaps: End-to-end test that provenance fails when upload artifact-digest metadata disagrees with a tampered download while per-file hashes still accidentally align (transport fidelity).
Promotion test asserting cli-reference/tui-reference/cask gate receipts are rejected when they omit bindings that native/* receipts already enforce.
Workflow test that release build fails if github.sha and inputs.source_sha diverge when identity checks are bypassed or regressed (contract-only simulation).
